claims.claim: Born 27 August 1981 in Toronto, Ontario
claims.note: Wikidata lists date of birth 27 August 1981 and place of birth Toronto.

claims.claim: Best known for playing Mike Ross, the lead in the USA legal drama Suits
claims.note: USC profile says best known for the leading role of Mike Ross on Suits; TV Series Finale lists network USA.

claims.claim: USC profile lists film work such as Old School and Pillow Talk
claims.note: Both titles appear in the film credits on the USC page.

claims.claim: Suits ran on USA from 23 June 2011 to 25 September 2019, nine seasons and 134 episodes
claims.note: Dates June 23, 2011 to September 25, 2019; seasons nine; episodes 134.

claims.claim: Role brought a Screen Actors Guild Award nomination for outstanding actor in a drama series
claims.note: USC page states the SAG Award nomination for outstanding actor in a drama series.

claims.claim: Adams left Suits after its seventh season
claims.note: TVLine: exited the show after seven seasons.

claims.claim: 2018 Hollywood Reporter interview: 'we've told his story and if he hangs out longer, Mike is just going to be another lawyer on television'
claims.note: Quoted verbatim in the Just Jared article, which introduces it as a 2018 interview.

claims.claim: Began to think about leaving at the end of the first half of season six
claims.note: Quoted: 'I started thinking about leaving at the end of the first half of season six'.

claims.claim: On Dinner's On Me he said he had not been taking good care of his mental health and had been drinking too much by the end of season seven
claims.note: Quoted: 'I wasn't taking good care of my mental health, and I was drinking too much [by] the end of Season 7'. Podcast named.

claims.claim: Only reason to stay was money; he never regretted leaving; 'It was the right thing for my marriage... It was time'
claims.note: Article quotes 'the only reason to stay was... money', 'I never regretted the decision for a second', and 'It was the right thing for my marriage... It was time.'

claims.claim: Wife is the actress Troian Bellisario
claims.note: Article identifies the now-wife as Pretty Little Liars' Troian Bellisario.

claims.claim: FAQ and body: in a 2018 interview he linked years of long stretches away from home and from his wife to leaving Suits
claims.note: Source: 'After seven seasons - really, eight years of being away from home and away from my now-wife ... and there was that pressure.' Given as a reason for leaving.

claims.claim: Cast as Major John Glenn in The Right Stuff, the Disney+ series about the Mercury Seven
claims.note: D23 names Patrick J. Adams as Major John Glenn and the Disney+ premiere; Mercury Seven is referenced. The article does not state the series is about them in those words, but the subject is clear.

claims.claim: Had 'the luxury of an enormous amount of resources'
claims.note: Exact quote in D23 interview.

claims.claim: John Glenn archives at Ohio State University are 'hundreds and hundreds of boxes of stuff'
claims.note: Exact wording in D23 article. Edited to attribute the description to the archives rather than to Adams.

claims.claim: Read Glenn's private letters, journal entries and correspondence with presidents; kept material as his 'linchpins' instead of an impression
claims.note: D23 quotes him on 'linchpins' and 'do an impression of John Glenn'.

claims.claim: 'I think I was the first person cast'
claims.note: Exact quote in TVLine.

claims.claim: 'I had a lot of fear, to be honest'
claims.note: Exact quote in TVLine.

claims.claim: Glenn as 'the odd man out of the Mercury Seven, and not because he was the best'
claims.note: Exact wording in TVLine.

claims.claim: 'I was looking to go to sleep for about 365 days'
claims.note: Exact quote in TVLine.

claims.claim: 'I just went, This is what I've been waiting for'
claims.note: TVLine: 'I just went, "This is what I've been waiting for,"'. The page quotes a verbatim fragment.

claims.claim: Broadway debut as Kippy Sunderstrom in the 2022 revival of Take Me Out
claims.note: Article: 'made his Broadway debut as Kippy Sunderstrom in the 2022 revival of the play'.

claims.claim: Take Me Out won the 2022 Tony for Best Revival of a Play, announced 12 June 2022; play closed the day before at the Hayes Theatre
claims.note: Article dated Jun. 12, 2022; 'closed yesterday, June 11, at the Hayes Theatre'.

claims.claim: Cast list in the same report includes Adams
claims.note: Cast list includes Patrick J. Adams.

claims.claim: The play has nude scenes; Adams said 'a play where we had to be naked every night'
claims.note: Article notes nude appearances; Adams's words: 'in a play where we had to be naked every night'.

claims.claim: 'It was so intense that I think I actually truly had to leave my body every night'
claims.note: Exact quote.

claims.claim: Director Scott Ellis encouraged him despite stage panic attacks, 'your chance to fix that, essentially'
claims.note: Source: 'But he said, this is your chance to fix that, essentially.' The quoted fragment is verbatim. Panic attacks are described in the article.

claims.claim: The Madison is a Paramount+ drama with Michelle Pfeiffer as Stacy Clyburn and Kurt Russell as Preston Clyburn
claims.note: Cast list confirms both roles and the Paramount+ original drama.

claims.claim: Adams plays Russell McIntosh; Russell is husband of Paige McIntosh (Elle Chapman), younger daughter of the Clyburns
claims.note: Source: Patrick J. Adams plays the husband of Paige McIntosh; Paige is the younger daughter.

claims.claim: Facebook page 'R.I.P. Patrick J. Adams' claimed death 'At about 11 a.m. ET on Thursday (October 29, 2026)'
claims.note: Quoted exactly.

claims.claim: Page gained nearly one million likes; skeptics noted no major Canadian network reported the death
claims.note: Source: 'nearly one million of likes'; 'had not been carried on any major Canadian network'.

claims.claim: On 30 October representatives said 'still alive and well, stop believing what you see on the Internet'
claims.note: Exact quote dated Friday, October 30, 2026.

claims.claim: Update dated 31 October 2026 says the story 'seems to be false'
claims.note: Source: 'UPDATE 31/10/2026 : This story seems to be false.'

claims.claim: FAQ: age 45 as of 31 October 2026 (born 27 August 1981)
claims.note: Date arithmetic is correct.

claims.claim: Citizenship: Canada
claims.note: Wikidata country of citizenship Canada; Mediamass calls him a Canadian actor.

valueNote: Sections follow the reader's questions (age, death hoax, why he left Suits, Glenn prep, Broadway debut). Corrects the false death report with dated primary wording.
summary: All claims checked against opened sources. The previously flagged FAQ wife answer and Ellis quote are supported verbatim; the Glenn archive and nude-scene attribution were corrected.
